chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Taylisi al-Khazzaz al-Kufi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Allah, our Lord, the Mighty and Exalted, was ever-present with knowledge as His Essence and not as something known, hearing as His Essence and not as something heard, sight as His Essence and not as something seen, and power as His Essence and not as something acted upon. When He created the things, and He was the Known, knowledge descended from Him upon the known, hearing upon the heard, sight upon the seen, and power upon the acted upon. I asked: 'So was Allah always Speaking?' He replied: 'Verily, speech is an originated attribute, not eternal. Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, existed when there was no Speaker.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's essential attributes and His created attributes in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Mu'tazili-influenced Shia doctrine of *sifat dhatiyyah* (essential attributes) being identical to the Divine Essence prior to creation, distinguishing them from *sifat fi'liyyah* (attributes of action). It specifically clarifies that while attributes like Knowledge and Power are eternal and intrinsic, Speech (*Kalam*) is an originated attribute (*hadith*), meaning Allah existed in a state of non-speech before His utterance, a key point in debates over whether the Quran is created or uncreated. This distinction underscores the transcendence of God's essence while affirming the reality of His attributes as they relate to the cosmos.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn `Ali Majilwayh (rh) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said on the authority Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi al-Khazzaz al-Kufi on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya on the authority of Ibn Muskan on the authority of Abu Basir that Abu 'Abdillah (AS) said:

Even in His Essence, and before anything existed, Allah, our Lord, the High and the Mighty, possessed all knowledge. Even in His Essence, and before a sound could be heard, He was All-Hearing. Even in His Essence, when there was nothing to be seen, He was All-Seeing. Even in His Essence, when there was no physical existence, He was Omnipotent. Although they existed prior to creation, it was only creation that these attributes manifested themselves: His Hearing upon the heard, His Seeing upon the seen, and His Omnipotence over the physical world. He says: I asked, “Then, Allah was not a Speaker?” He (AS) replied, “Verily, speech is an originated [muhdathah] attribute and not eternal [azaliyyah]. Allah, the Mighty and High, existed when no speakers existed.”
